extracted.intended_audience: university instructional designers, educational technologists, administrators, and IT managers planning or managing online learning systems
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, organizing, selecting components for, and governing an institution-scale online learning system (LMS/CMS/portal/SIS/infrastructure) so it supports intended students and learning outcomes and can evolve over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the needs of intended learners, curriculum, and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Before embarking on development, careful stock needs to be taken of the needs of the intended learners, the curriculum to be offered, and the context for the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for internal and external environmental factors (competing priorities, budgets, faculty/student preparedness, professional requirements). Use these to drive planning and organizational decisions rather than assuming a one-size-fits-all approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design from two fundamental vantage points
rubrics_metrics.description: All teaching and learning systems should be built from two vantage points: the needs of the intended students, and the intended learning outcomes of the course or program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use students' needs (prior learning, tech access, expectations) and clearly stated intended learning outcomes (knowledge, skills, attributes) as the primary determinants of course design, assessment, and system functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand student preparedness and access
rubrics_metrics.description: For intended students, understand their prior learning, background with technology, expectations, financial/resources availability, access to web/networks, bandwidth limitations, and other preparedness factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make judgement calls about balancing common, efficient solutions with accommodations for individual needs (e.g., assume high-bandwidth but provide alternative access like CD-ROMs/DVDs for those without).

rubrics_metrics.name: State clear intended learning outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a need for clear identification of the intended learning outcomes of any course, program, or training event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes inform assessment design, recognition of prior learning, curriculum linkage, and the required online learning functionality. In applied fields this is routine; in academic fields outcomes must be defined precisely to drive system design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for size, scope, and scalability
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide on the size, scope, and scalability needed—whether delivery is to a defined cohort once a year or made available to all comers at all times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scalability decisions strongly impact system architecture, resourcing, and support requirements; plan accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept that real systems deviate from the ideal and must be adaptable
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideal system assumes no restrictions; a real system will face limited resources, legacy systems, staff retraining needs, unworkable policies, inadequate governance, and evolving pedagogical understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design infrastructure that can change constantly to accommodate evolving curriculum, technologies, and student needs; manage inevitable deviations pragmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish clear governance and organizational structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Without effective structures and processes, selection, deployment, and ongoing performance of an online learning system will be challenging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define roles, responsibilities, and processes to balance centralization vs decentralization and to resolve conflicts over discipline ownership, control, and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance centralization versus decentralization
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide how much to foster random experimentation versus tight control through a centralized system; this decision should be driven by mission, mandate, values, architecture, and finances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralization improves integration, security, and reduced duplication; decentralization favors innovation and discipline-specific needs. Choose and resource accordingly, understanding political and practical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt an overall framework linking outcomes to components
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate learning outcomes into course content and resources plus teaching strategies, then into courseware stored on a CMS and delivered via an LMS interfaced with library, services, SIS, secure server, and a user portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a conceptual framework (components: learning outcomes, courseware development team, LMS, library/digital resources, services, SIS, secure server, user portal, quality assessment) to plan integration and workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble an appropriate development team and plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a preliminary proposal that lays out objectives, intended student market, and proposed approach, and identify the composition of development and delivery teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams range from a single skilled content expert to complex teams including instructional designers, editors, visual/multimedia designers, programmers, and systems staff. Include project management practices appropriate to scope and cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose an appropriate Learning Management System (LMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select between commercial/proprietary LMSs and in-house/open-source solutions based on the needs of the course and institution, not just cost or legacy constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider training needs, support, interoperability, lock-in costs, community support for open-source, and back-end system implications. Use independent evaluations where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use explicit evaluative criteria for LMS selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop evaluative criteria to guide LMS selection and try out candidate applications under those headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Athabasca used: Mandate; Systems Administration; Cost; Instructional Design; Teaching and Learning Tools. A transparent, broad-based selection process helps gain institutional acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a Content Management System (CMS) suited to courseware needs
rubrics_metrics.description: A CMS should manage web content and provide a secure, accessible, collaborative environment for creation and storage of content in XML format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose between web content management and document management systems; ensure CMS and LMS are technologically compatible and integrated for seamless user experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate library and digital resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Link the LMS to necessary online resources (institutional/public libraries, gateways, digital databases, and repositories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure availability or anticipation of resources during courseware development; leverage librarians' expertise in knowledge management and intellectual property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide comprehensive learner services
rubrics_metrics.description: Give priority to non-academic learner support such as technical help, educational advising, counselling, and services for learners with special needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop these services in concert with curriculum and ensure they're adapted from traditional environments to online delivery, with capacity to evolve with expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure robust SIS–LMS integration and identity management
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideally link the LMS to the Student Information System so the right student is auto-enrolled with correct information available to instructors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integration avoids manual entry errors; instructors need capabilities to manage marks and communication. Multiple LMSs in an institution require careful interfacing and authentication systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a user portal enabling single secure login and personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: The portal should allow a learner, with one secure login, to access LMS, grades, student files, learner services, and personalize their interface and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portals enable e-portfolios, social networking, course support, and future automated supports (e-advising/e-counselling). Personalization improves student experience and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan independent and structured quality assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a plan for independent evaluation of the system, especially the degree to which it enables achievement of stated learning outcomes and user satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent quality assessment should examine ROI and hidden implementation costs; evaluations must be structured and comparable to guide improvement or decommissioning decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate and maintain back-end hardware and connectivity needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate servers, switches, and connectivity up front and adjust as users grow; set uptime expectations (typically 24/7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate increasing video use and plan backend capacity accordingly; routine adjustment and monitoring are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish policies for server access, security, and system use
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies must balance stability and security with the need to innovate in the online learning system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop access rules, security standards, and acceptable-use policies to protect systems while enabling pedagogical innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide technical help, training, orientation, and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical help and helpdesk support should be linked to training, orientation, and documentation to support students and staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify mandates and lines of responsibility to avoid duplication or gaps; consider distributed vs centralized support models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address human resource issues and working conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider collective agreements, employment contracts, service standards, expectations beyond traditional hours, and integration of online activities into accepted practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt hiring, promotion, position classification, and professional development to the dynamic nature of online learning work to retain staff and avoid exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for workforce skill development and flexible career paths
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize staff may evolve into key online roles without formal training; institutions should invest in training and flexible HR practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop inter/intra-institutional support groups, learning communities, and opportunities for staff development to sustain the system long-term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure decision-making and resource-allocation processes carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: When establishing committees or decision bodies, balance contributors who know the technology, central technical staff, decentralized technical staff, central administration, and users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent and thorough evaluation inputs are important to prevent biased or politically driven decisions; ensure accountability and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage organizational change deliberately
rubrics_metrics.description: Change must be managed so that curriculum, technologies, and student expectations are updated without causing systemic disruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance adopting new ideas/products versus sticking with established systems; centralization/decentralization choices affect how change is implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bifurcated development of academic and administrative computing
rubrics_metrics.description: Separation of academic and administrative computing assumes technological separation; interdependencies make joint vision for architecture critical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jointly develop technological architecture to provide flexibility and sustainability; bifurcated development risks compromised student services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize interoperability and reusability standards limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for online learning interoperability and reusability are being developed but the promise has not yet been fully met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about lock-in and migrating content; plan for standards where possible but expect practical constraints and organizational relearning costs.
